text:
Anya: Quick review request
I added a "compact summary" above the notify preview that shows the effective recipients for the current rule (e.g. "Notifying: Email, Slack (suppressed)"). Prototype: https://figma.com/file/compact-summary-1799

Kevin: Nice idea. A couple thoughts: 1) the summary reads first for sighted users, but SR users need it announced too when the preview loads. 2) how do we avoid duplication if SR also reads each pill?

Mina: For screen readers I'd suggest a short live region announcement only on initial load or after a user action that changes routing (not on every background poll). Make it: "Preview updated: notifying Email and Slack (Slack suppressed)". Keep it short.

Olga: Visual: the summary pill currently truncates long service names and shows "...". We should expose the full text with aria-describedby and a tooltip on focus/hover. Also ensure the summary pill is keyboard focusable and included in reading order before the list.

Anya: Good. Also copy: product wants "Suppressed" rather than "Muted". I'll change the tag text.

Kevin: Accessibility: when a channel is suppressed because of a quiet window or schedule, the pill should be visually disabled and include an explanatory sublabel (small text) like "Suppressed by schedule". For SR, include that in aria-label: "Slack, suppressed by schedule".

Mina: Implementation note: if we virtualize the channel list we must not rely on list-indexed announcements. Keep a dedicated live region for user actions (snooze, unsnooze, threshold change) and a separate offscreen summary element that SR can read on demand with a simple link "Read preview summary" for users who want details.

Olga: On keyboard flow: tab should land on the summary pill first, then to the first channel pill, then through actions. If the summary pill opens a quick panel with details, focus should move into the panel's first control and return on close. Escape closes panel and returns focus. We'll document that.

Anya: Contrast: the summary uses a semi-transparent white on blue (12px). Axe flagged 3:1. Let's bump weight or darken text to pass 4.5:1. If customers use custom channel colors, runtime contrast calc should pick a readable foreground or fallback to outline.

Kevin: Copy nit: for quick actions use verbs like "Snooze" not "Mute". Inline tooltips should match final copy (avoid internal flags names). Also include duration in announcement: "Snoozed Slack for 30 minutes".

Mina: Edge case: when the routing rules are complex (multiple recipients with selector logic), summarizing might mislead. Maybe show "Notifying: Email + 2 others" with a button "View details" that opens the expanded preview. That keeps the summary small and avoids overload.

Olga: That sounds good for mobile too. On small widths the summary should compress to "Email +2" and the details button should be accessible via keyboard and SR-friendly.

Anya: Next steps: I'll update the Figma to use "Suppressed" copy, add an offscreen aria-describedby for the full summary, and adjust contrast. Mina, can you draft the live-region rules? Kevin, can you pair on the focus return behaviour? Olga, check translations for long labels?

Kevin: I can pair after 3pm.

Mina: I'll write the live-region spec and debounce rules (only announce after 200ms idle and batch multiple changes).

Olga: I'll run translations through German and Japanese samples and test truncation.

A11y-bot: Accessibility checklist: summary is focusable and announced on load/user action, aria-describedby exposes full text, dedicated user-action live region (debounced), aria-label includes status and reason, focus management for details panel (trap on open, return on close), contrast >= 4.5:1, test with virtualized list + do not rely on DOM index, run axe + NVDA manual pass.

Anya: Thanks all  will post updated mock and an interaction spec tomorrow morning.
